generator_definition.key_material: 32-byte CSPRNG key generated once by the generation executor, committed as SHA256(key) in this registration BEFORE any case is generated; raw key sealed with the generation executor, disclosed to reviewers only after execution approval
generator_definition.per_case_stream: Use executable_spec exclusively: domain-separated HMAC-SHA256, with a per-item counter shared by all draws; language excluded.
generator_definition.likert: Use unbiased uniform(5) from executable_spec; answer=1+value
generator_definition.multi_choice: Use executable_spec; no independent modulo-only algorithm
generator_definition.conditional_other_text: left empty (not part of scoring surface; see P09 retention-contract)
generator_definition.why_not_periodic: the periodic generator makes seeds 1001-1011 share 47/56 item responses with development seeds 1-11 (measured on data/questions.json at a4aff902); seed number difference is not content separation
generator_definition.language_rule: one answer vector per seed_id; the same vector is rendered in ko and in en. KO/EN are two outputs of the same case, not two cases. Language equivalence (translation parity of rendered text) is a separate check with its own scope record and is not part of SEP checks.

executable_spec.key: 32 random bytes from OS CSPRNG (node crypto.randomBytes(32)); commitment = sha256(key) hex, registered before generation; key sealed with custodian
executable_spec.domain_separation: HMAC-SHA256 message = 'Q90-E-FINAL-v1' || 0x00 || uint32be(seed_id) || 0x00 || utf8(item_id) || 0x00 || uint32be(counter); counter starts at 0 per (seed_id,item_id) and increments on every additional draw (multi-choice picks, rejection retries)
executable_spec.integer_conversion: take first 8 bytes of the 32-byte HMAC output as uint64 big-endian = r In JavaScript use BigInt for r, 2^64, limit and modulo; convert bounded final option index to Number only after range check. Number arithmetic on uint64 is prohibited.
executable_spec.uniform_modulo_rejection: for range n: limit = floor(2^64 / n) * n; if r >= limit -> increment counter, redraw; else value = r mod n. Guarantees exact uniformity, no modulo bias
executable_spec.item_order: items iterated in data/questions.json order: sections[].questions[] flattened, exactly as prototype-tests.cjs L13 (core = q.sections.flatMap(s=>s.questions)); item_id = question.id
executable_spec.single_choice: n = len(options) in questions.json order; answer = options[value]
executable_spec.multi_choice: k = 1 + uniform(min(question.max || 1, options.length)); remaining indices initially [0,...,options.length-1]; for each of k draws: j=uniform(remaining.length), select remaining[j], then splice j from remaining without reordering other entries. Each draw and rejection advances the shared item counter. Sort selected indices ascending; answers are options at those indices. No reset of counter between k and selections.
executable_spec.conditional_other_text: left empty; otherId fields not populated
executable_spec.language: NOT an input to any HMAC; the same answer object is passed to the engines with lang='ko' and lang='en'
executable_spec.reference_implementation: to be written by generation_executor as a single-file script; its sha256 registered with the vectors; peer re-runs it from key + this spec and must reproduce all 24 answer_vector_sha256 values
executable_spec.invalid_schema: Empty options, invalid max, duplicate item ids, unsupported question type, unsafe seed/counter or counter exhaustion abort registration as input/spec error. No coercion/silent fallback. Explicit absence of max uses 1, matching declared spec; validation before generation.
executable_spec.publishedAt_binding: Verified on frozen program-engine.js: build(opts) at1262, opts.publishedAt at1271, formatted at1843 and2900. Pass opts.publishedAt explicitly as registered ISO constant; exact evaluated release must be reverified before execution.

role_separation.ai_only_diagnostic: automated/AI-executed technical tests MAY produce raw metrics in track E (hashes, pass/fail counts, mismatch lists) per v1 tracks.E; these raw metrics are admissible as A5.1/A5.2 support evidence with source_origin=internal_software_test. What AI may NOT do: replace the human final judgment of a rubric level, act as a rater/adjudicator, or stand in for participants. Cells with rater_type=ai_only_diagnostic do not enter confirmed grades.
role_separation.identity_evidence: roster record (role, stable_actor_id, verification source, date, verifier) kept by the editor; hash proves the roster was fixed before generation; the roster plus the direct id check proves the persons are distinct. Real names may remain unfilled until G13; see who_fixes_what. Different accounts alone do not establish different people: the human verifier attests actual-person distinctness and records conflicts privately; hash/IDs cannot replace that attestation.

A hash comparison does not satisfy this; the check is on the ids themselves and is recorded with the roster.

repetition_rules.rule: each of the 48 final outputs (24 vectors x 2 languages) is generated twice by two different executors, on the same release_sha, same engine_bundle_sha256, same frozen clock, same TZ. Both raw_output_sha256 and canonical_output_sha256 are stored for every product (96 products).
repetition_rules.pass: raw_output_sha256 identical 48/48 across the two runs (REQUIRED, because the clock is frozen so the three time paths are constant) AND canonical_output_sha256 identical 48/48. Any raw mismatch is an unexplained same-condition mismatch candidate (v1 zero_required) and blocks registration of outputs.

canonicalization_exact.purpose: diagnostic and for cross-comparison with runs made under a non-frozen clock; NOT used to rescue a raw mismatch in the frozen-clock runs
canonicalization_exact.source_locations: assets/js/report-engine.js L1867 (return {..., generatedAt}), assets/js/report-engine-v4.js L9379 (report._v4Meta.generatedAt), assets/js/program-engine.js L2899 (meta.generatedAt) at a4aff902

repetition_rules.rule: one rater re-scores 4 randomly drawn final cases >= 7 days after first scoring; exact agreement threshold reuses v1 80%; failure marks that rater's data 'calibration_required' (not deleted, not re-scored by the same rater without re-calibration) Re-score materials receive fresh random blinded labels and randomized order; original raw ratings remain locked, original labels hidden until comparison.

dispute_procedure.definition: Any item level disagreement (including 1 level) or measured/missing/blocked status disagreement is reviewed by the third human, per execution_plan.raters. A >=2-level gap also fails the operational agreement threshold before adjudication.
dispute_procedure.adjudicator: Pre-registered third human R1 or R2, verified distinct from both raters by the roster and direct ID check; hash difference alone is insufficient.
dispute_procedure.adjudicator_input: Evidence quotes and anchor citations plus disputed cell provided; rater identities withheld. Levels may be inferred from anchors, so no score-blindness claim; adjudicator records an independent anchor-based decision and rationale.
dispute_procedure.decision_rule: select ONE level by anchor text comparison; averaging prohibited; if neither rater has evidence, cell -> missing
dispute_procedure.record: append-only: rater_1 level, rater_2 level, adjudicated level, reason, timestamp
dispute_procedure.anchor_defect_path: if the dispute stems from ambiguous anchor wording, record in anchor_defect_ledger for v2; no score change in the current round

Prior failed run remains reportable.
